data.body:
Class-drain (operator-approved Step-7 extension): the package-location repo-root defect CLASS is now structurally gated in CI, not just fixed instance-by-instance.

WHY A SIBLING GUARD, NOT AN EXTENSION OF THE EXISTING ONE
The existing guard `scripts/check_repo_root_from_tracker.py` (wired into `make lint`) drains ONE spelling of this class: deriving the code root from the STORE path, `dirname(<tracker>)`. Its AST visitor keys on the `os.path.dirname(<store-expr>)` composition. The reconciler defect is the OTHER spelling — deriving the code root from the PACKAGE LOCATION, `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[N]`. Those are structurally unrelated AST shapes, so extending the tracker guard's visitor to also match `parents[N]` would have fused two unrelated detectors into one and made each harder to reason about. Per the operator's sanctioned fork, I added a SIBLING guard of the SAME kind instead: `scripts/check_repo_root_from_package.py`, mirroring the tracker guard's architecture (AST visitor, `# repo-root-ok:` / `# repo-root-seam:` sanction markers with mandatory reasons, unparseable-source-is-a-violation, wired into `make lint`).

OBSERVABLE INVARIANT, NOT A CHANGE-DETECTOR
The guard asserts the invariant "the reconciler repo root is resolved through the one validated resolver, never re-derived raw from the package location." It flags only the AST SUBSCRIPT root-climb `Path(__file__)[.resolve()/.absolute()].parents[<n>]`. It is NOT a source-text grep and NOT symbol-name-based, so it survives benign renames and refactors. Discrimination is pinned by the self-tests:
- FLAGGED: `Path(__file__).parents[2]`, `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]`, `str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4])`, module-qualified `pathlib.Path(...)`, and the construct nested inside a boolean fallback (`env or Path(__file__)...parents[4]`).
- NOT flagged: the singular `Path(__file__).parent` package-data idiom (an attribute access, ~50 legitimate sites locating package data — a DIFFERENT construct), a `config.reconciler_repo_root()` call, `parents[N]` on a non-`__file__` path, and docstrings/comments (they compose nothing and never reach the AST).

This narrowness is empirically grounded: src-wide, the `.resolve().parents[N]` subscript root-climb appears in only TWO real code sites, while the singular `.parent` attribute appears ~50 times — so a guard keyed on the subscript shape is inherently low-false-positive.

THE TWO SANCTIONED SITES (both genuine non-defects, each documented with a reason)
1. `src/rebar/config.py` — `# repo-root-seam:` on the `parents[2]` candidate inside `reconciler_repo_root()`. This is THE validated resolver: the candidate is used ONLY after `_is_repo_checkout()` confirms a real checkout, else it falls back to the validated cwd git-toplevel, else raises. Every reconciler surface routes through it.
2. `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py` — `# repo-root-ok:` on the `parents[3]` package PARENT prepended to `sys.path`. That is an install-location-relative path (correct under editable AND wheel installs) and is not treated as a checkout root; it never binds `repo_root`.

A self-test (`test_the_only_sanctioned_sites_are_the_resolver_seam_and_the_pkg_parent`) asserts those are the ONLY two sanctioned `.parents[` sites in `src/`, so a future third sanction — i.e. someone parking a new raw derivation behind a marker instead of routing through the resolver — fails CI. Verified: the guard passes clean on the drained tree (exit 0) and flags a reintroduced raw fetcher-style instance (exit 1).

Result: the fetcher siblings are fixed to route through the resolver, and any NEW package-location root-climb anywhere under `src/` now fails `make lint` — the class is drained, not just this instance.
